transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we begin, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I've been having this issue when I talk. I'm a retail supervisor, and lately, when I try to explain things like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule to my team, my words just start jumping around. 

I'll go from talking about the delivery trucks to Thursdays, and then suddenly I'm on about the church grill or my boss’s tone of voice. I don't really mean to do it, but... well, people just stare at me like they completely can’t follow what I’m saying. It's making it really hard to do my job.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, energetic, or elated, or that you need much less sleep than usual?

No, I... I haven't noticed anything like that. I definitely wouldn't say I feel unusually energetic or elated. Honestly, I just feel normal in that regard, maybe just a bit stressed out about the whole work situation. And my sleep is... well, it's about the same as usual. I definitely haven't felt like I can just skip sleeping or anything like that.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others find unusual or hard to accept?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or anything, and I don't think I have any unusual beliefs. It's really just the issue with my speech getting all jumbled up at work that's been bothering me.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, or other neurological symptoms like headaches, weakness, or memory problems around the time your speech difficulties started?

No, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or passed out... no seizures or anything. I don't really get headaches either, and my memory seems fine. I'm not feeling weak. It's just the talking thing. Physically, I feel completely normal.
Over these past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

No, not really. I haven't felt down or sad, no. I still enjoy my usual routine and everything. It's not really a mood issue... my mood is basically fine. I'm just dealing with the frustration of how my words are coming out at the store, but I definitely haven't lost interest in things.
Can you tell me exactly how long you've been noticing this jumbled, disorganized speech pattern - has it been going on for a few weeks, a couple of months, or longer?

It's been going on for a while now... longer than a few weeks. I'd say the jumbled explanations and, you know, those odd stops when I'm on the sales floor... it's been noticeable for about six months now.
Over these past six months, have you noticed yourself withdrawing from friends or family, feeling less motivated to do things, or showing less emotion than you used to?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I'm still seeing people and doing things the way I usually do. I don't feel unmotivated or... flat, I guess you'd call it. It's really just the speech thing that's been bothering me.

Besides the jumbled speech, have you or others noticed any unusual or disorganized behavior, such as acting oddly, having trouble completing tasks, or doing things that seem out of context for the situation?

Yeah, I suppose there have been a few things like that at work. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, I'll catch myself just pacing the same aisle. Or I'll be straightening the exact same row of batteries, just over and over again. And... well, there are times I'll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, not really doing anything, while the associates are just waiting for me to tell them what to do.

Over these past six months, have you or your supervisors noticed that your work performance or ability to manage your daily responsibilities has significantly declined because of these speech and behavior issues?

Yeah, it really has. At work... well, they just don't trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. I had a performance review recently, and my boss actually warned me that I could be suspended if things don't improve soon. 

And it's not just at the store, either. At home, my wife has had to start covering commitments that I usually handle. I guess... well, people just started getting uncomfortable or confused around me, so she's had to step in and take over for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates prominent disorganized speech (derailment/tangentiality) and disorganized behavior (repetitive purposeless actions, catatonic-like staring), present for approximately 6 months, causing significant functional decline at work and home. Mood episode criteria (mania, hypomania, depression) were explicitly denied, ruling out schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features. No neurological, substance, or medical etiology was identified. Negative symptoms (avolition, flat affect, social withdrawal) were not endorsed, and no clear hallucinations or delusions were elicited, but the presence of two Criterion A domains (disorganized speech and disorganized behavior) for the required duration with functional impairment supports a diagnosis of Schizophrenia, unspecified.
